<p align="center">
  <b>Castaway</b> (working title) · colly 01 of 05 · logo by wk of Strandline<br>
  <sub>an unofficial lo-fi remake, inspired by the 1992 desert-island screensaver Johnny Castaway · in development · no video published yet</sub>
</p>

**Castaway** is a ten-hour lo-fi video for YouTube in which almost nothing happens, on purpose. One young woman, one tiny island, one tall palm, a raft and a great deal of time. She idles, nodding along to the music in her headphones, and every so often something happens. She throws a message in a bottle out to sea, and it washes straight back to her feet. A delivery drone drops off a parcel, and the parcel is another pair of headphones. A coconut lands on a hermit crab, and the crab walks off wearing it. All of it hand-painted, sunny and coastal: 16:9, 1080p, 30 fps, always daytime.

**The schedule** lives in [activities.toml](activities.toml): more than 90 activities. Most run on four timers, from everyday routines every 2 to 5 minutes to super-rare ones every 3 to 6 hours; the rest are follow-ups that another activity sets off. Each one waits for the next bar of the music before it starts, so every gag lands on the beat. In a typical ten-hour run she is busy about a third of the time. The other two thirds are the product.

**The sound** is synthesized from code by [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py), every last bit of it: no samples, no stock loops, no recordings, more than 150 files. The theme is a seamless 60-second loop at 80 BPM in F major.

```sh
python tools/serve.py
# then dial http://127.0.0.1:8765/   (local calls only)
```

<p align="center"><sub>A web page with a live preview and an export to a YouTube-ready MP4, encoded frame-exact in the browser.<br>Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm packages. Cut along the dashes; the island is used to being cut off.</sub></p>

<br>

<p align="center">
  <img src="assets/47-ansi-logo-colly_opus_5.5-colly.svg" width="100%" alt="Four more ANSI block-letter logos on one black 80-column page, separated by dashed cut lines with bright blue cut here tags, each signed by a different artist of Strandline and numbered colly 02 to 05 of 05. DRONE, by cw/stl: squared chrome capitals shaded white to light grey to dark grey with light-cyan slivers, two rotors on short masts, their blades flickering between wide and narrow, the whole word hovering up and down; at the right the word headphones stacked six times and fading; tagline: a delivery drone, one parcel, inside it, another pair of headphones. SHARK, by lmp/stl: rounded capitals in light cyan, cyan and blue, the A drawn as a dorsal fin wearing headphones, the whole word nodding down on every beat; at the left, nod . nod . nod stacked and fading; tagline: a shark in headphones, nods on the beat, same playlist, apparently. CRAB, by cnc/stl: squat wide capitals in coral and red with yellow slivers, a brown coconut shell worn on the B, eight half-block legs underneath that kick out and tuck in, the word walking sideways a column per beat, four steps right and four back; at the right, click . clack stacked and fading; tagline: a coconut lands on a hermit crab, the crab keeps it, walks off in it. BOTTLE, by nau/stl: hollow outline letters traced in underscores, slashes and pipes, coloured row by row from light green to cyan, bobbing on a hatched blue slab with dotted rules out to both edges; tagline: she throws a bottle, it washes straight back, later, a reply. At the bottom, a cut line tagged end of colly, the artists wk, cw, lmp, cnc and nau of Strandline, and the line: no samples were harmed.">
</p>

**What a colly was.** In the 1990s an ANSI art group would release one long text file stacking the logos it had drawn for different bulletin boards, with a cut line between each one so every sysop could snip out their own. Every letter was built by hand from full and half blocks and shaded through ░ ▒ ▓ between two or three neighbouring colours, with an accent hue tucked into the counters, the artist's tag over the first letter and the board's phone number underneath, repeated and fading.

**This one** stacks five: the island, then two of its couriers and two of its regular callers, each by a different artist with their own letterforms, their own colours and one small move on the beat. The drone hovers. The shark nods. The crab walks sideways. The bottle bobs. The island stays exactly where it is, which is the whole idea. Its number is on page one, 127.0.0.1:8765, and it only takes local calls.

**Drawn letter by letter, honestly.** Every letter really is drawn on its own, pixel by pixel, in the generator: the three A's in CASTAWAY are three different A's, and the R in DRONE has nothing to do with the R in SHARK or the one in CRAB. A Node script then turns each pair of pixel rows into ▀ ▄ █ cells, shades them row by row and writes one path per colour, with the shade characters as the same 25, 50 and 75 percent dot patterns a VGA text screen draws.

</details>

<summary><b>THE SMALL PRINT</b> · the timers, the sound, the tools, credits and greetz</summary>

```text
 THE TIMERS · as of 2026-10-01 · default run 10:00:00, seed 1992
 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  regular ......... every 2 to 5 minutes ......... about 155 a run
  occasional ...... every 12 to 25 minutes ....... about 30
  rare ............ every 30 to 60 minutes ....... about 13
  super rare ...... every 3 to 6 hours ........... about 2, never over 3
  chained ......... follow-ups, started by another activity
 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  typical counts are the median of 200 simulated ten-hour runs. every
  start snaps to the next bar of the music (3 s). lanes let things
  overlap, so a ship can sail past while she is busy with a coconut.
  it waits for her to get busy first. it has the timing of a pro

 THE SOUND · every file synthesized from code
  theme ........... seamless 60 s loop: 80 BPM, F major, ii-V-I-vi,
                    20 bars of exactly 3 s. electric piano, kalimba
                    lead, soft drums, vinyl surface noise
  ocean ........... also a seamless 60 s loop
  levels .......... -14 LUFS, true peak at or below -1 dBTP, adjustable
                    in master and per routine
  samples ......... 0     stock loops ..... 0     recordings ..... 0
  listened to ..... not yet. the numbers look lovely on paper

 THE TOOLS
  python tools/serve.py ............ the renderer: live preview at
                                     http://127.0.0.1:8765/ and export
                                     to a YouTube-ready MP4
  python tools/schedule.py ......... checks the schedule, simulates a
                                     ten-hour run
  python tools/render_demo.py --dev  a dev reel of every activity with
                                     a heads-up display (the older
                                     Python reference renderer)
  python tools/make_audio.py ....... makes every sound
  export: frame-exact H.264 in the browser (WebCodecs, 68 to 78 frames
  a second at 1080p30 in Chrome), then the server mixes in the sound
  and joins the two into one MP4

 CREDITS
  logos ........... wk (CASTAWAY, ROSTER), cw (DRONE), lmp (SHARK),
                    cnc (CRAB), nau (BOTTLE), all five of Strandline
  inspired by ..... Johnny Castaway (1992), which belongs to its
                    owners. this is an unofficial remake, in spirit
  the style ....... the PC ANSI logo collies of the 1990s, and the
                    groups still drawing them today. nothing of theirs
                    is copied: no letters, no logos, no names, no numbers

 GREETZ
  everyone who ever cut a logo out of a colly with a text editor ·
  every sysop who kept a node open for one more caller ·
  the tide, for the honest reviews
```
